base-converter.quickAnswer: Type a number, pick the from-base and to-base (2 to 36), and get the converted value instantly. FF in base 16 = 255 in base 10; 255 in base 10 = 11111111 in base 2. Digits that do not belong to the chosen base show a clear error.
keyFacts: Base = how many distinct digits: binary 2, octal 8, decimal 10, hex 16.
Digits go 0-9 then A-Z, so base 36 uses all letters.
Computers store everything in binary (base 2); hex is its compact shorthand.
Colour codes (#FF0000), memory addresses and Unicode code points are all hex.
Octal (base 8) survives in Unix file permissions like 755.
Leading zeros are fine: 0FF₁₆ and FF₁₆ are the same number.
howTo: Choose the base it is written in (2-36).
Read the converted result plus its decimal value instantly.
base-converter.formula:
To decimal: sum of digit × base^position (positions from the right, starting at 0).
From decimal: repeated division by the target base, reading remainders bottom-up.
Example: FF₁₆ = 15×16¹ + 15×16⁰ = 240 + 15 = 255.
base-converter.workedExample:
Convert FF (hex) to decimal:
1. From-base 16, digits F=15, F=15.
2. 15 × 16 + 15 = 240 + 15 = 255.
Convert 255 (decimal) to binary:
1. Repeated ÷2: 255→127 r1, 127→63 r1, 63→31 r1, 31→15 r1, 15→7 r1, 7→3 r1, 3→1 r1, 1→0 r1.
2. Read remainders upward: 11111111₂.

faqs.q: How do I convert hex to decimal?
faqs.a: Multiply each hex digit by 16^position and add. FF = 15×16 + 15 = 255. Or type it here: number FF, from-base 16, to-base 10.

faqs.q: How do I convert decimal to binary?
faqs.a: Repeatedly divide by 2 and record remainders, then read them bottom-up. 13 → 1101. This tool does it instantly for any base 2-36.
Binary (2) for storage and logic, hexadecimal (16) as its readable shorthand, and octal (8) in niches like Unix permissions. Decimal (10) is for humans.

faqs.q: Why is my conversion showing an error?
faqs.a: A digit does not belong to the from-base - e.g. "2" in binary, or "G" in hex. Check the from-base matches how your number is actually written.
Compact human-readable IDs: 0-9 plus A-Z gives short strings. URL shorteners and some ticket/serial systems use base-36 or similar encodings.
Yes - 0x is just a prefix meaning "hex follows". Type the number with or without it here; both convert identically.

labels.invalidNumber: Invalid number for the selected base. Check the digits.

mistakes: Using letters beyond your base — 'G' is invalid in hex, and 'Z' only exists in bases 27 and up. The tool errors instead of guessing, so check the from-base.
Forgetting what base a pasted number is in — '755' as octal (Unix permissions) is 493 in decimal, but 755 as decimal is just 755. Same digits, different value.
This tool handles whole numbers only. Don't feed it fractions like 101.11 or expect a decimal point in the answer.
Converting hex→decimal, then reading that decimal answer as hex again, is the classic double-conversion error — convert once, then read.
Numbers beyond about 9 × 10¹⁵ lose precision in conversion. Split huge values into chunks instead.
